A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-J. Text comparison and rendered-page checks support a reliable comparison, including the appendices.

before.justification: v4 reports original data-attribution experiments, including LDS comparisons, counterfactual retraining, qualitative examples, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experimental results and presents replacement qualitative attribution examples in Figure 1.

M1.justification: The influence-function framework, GGN approximations, recommended EK-FAC configuration, gradient compression, query batching, and measurement functions remain unchanged in Section 3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-2, CIFAR-10, ArtBench-10, and the same dequantised CIFAR settings. Figure 1 switches to ArtBench examples, but ArtBench was already evaluated in v4, including Figure 2 and Appendix J.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains TRAK, D-TRAK, CLIP similarity, and the exact-retraining oracle. Figure 3 retains TRAK, D-TRAK, and random removal as comparators. Appendix comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The model configurations, LDS subset construction, retraining procedures, removal fractions, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged. Figure 1 changes the displayed qualitative examples without documenting a revision to the benchmark protocols or evaluation sample sizes.

E4.justification: Figure 1 replaces the CIFAR-10 qualitative case study with ArtBench examples showing generated samples alongside top, neutral, and negative training influences. This changes the illustrative evidence for perceptual relevance; the quantitative ablations and failure analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The five-seed retraining ensembles in Appendix J.6 and standard-error reporting in Figures 2-3 are retained. No repeated-run information, uncertainty reporting, or statistical estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: Figure 1 replaces five CIFAR-10 sample-attribution examples with six ArtBench examples absent from v4. These are different qualitative results, not evidence of a same-setting performance gain. Quantitative scores, rankings, ablation plots, and runtime and memory results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations in Sections 2-3 and Appendices A-C, complexity analysis in Appendix E, and augmentation formulations in Appendix J.9 remain unchanged. Opening-page reflow does not alter the equations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about scalable influence functions, unifying previous approaches, and improved attribution performance without method-specific hyperparameter tuning.

C2.justification: Sections 4.1 and 5 and Appendix H preserve the same interpretations and limitations concerning measurement proxies, inaccurate numerical predictions, loss-change asymmetry, and stability across training subsets. The replacement illustration adds no substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information, data processing, and code-access information remain unchanged, including Appendices E and J.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged, including Appendix D's comparison with previous diffusion-attribution methods. The added G-Research acknowledgment is a funding credit, not a related-work addition.

P1.justification: v5 adds a sentence acknowledging a G-Research grant, updates Figure 1's dataset name, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose and section sequence are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 changes from five CIFAR-10 rows to six ArtBench rows while retaining the influence-group layout. It moves from page 3 to page 2, reflowing the introduction and background. All other figures and tables, including those in the appendices, remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The ArtBench illustration replaces an existing qualitative demonstration within already covered datasets, and the acknowledgment adds funding credit. Quantitative validation, technical explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged. These limited edits leave the paper's overall explanatory and evidential quality essentially unchanged.
